messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: wavelet transform plot
parts:
Hi all-

the following code produces a plot of a wavelet transform. In the
following message I'll post the (toy) data which is used in the plot.

I'm looking for advice on how to do several things.:

1. flip the y/scale axis while preserving the over all look (i've not
had success with this)
2. improving the look of the tiling. there are often lines in the
tiling, does this result from using POSIXct x-axis? and the color
(lines) doesnt jive with the fill (probably due to alpha).
3. any other advice, e.g. perhaps improving the look of the shaded
cone-of-influence.

Thanks for your consideration.

James

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: Re: wavelet transform plot
parts:
here's the code

size=0
siglvl=.95
gg.wave <- ggplot( wave.frame ) +
geom_tile( aes(x=time, y=period, fill=power,
colour=power, alpha=coi), size=size ) +
geom_contour( aes(x=time, y=period,
z=signif), color='white', breaks=siglvl ) +
scale_fill_continuous(low="black",
high="red") +
scale_colour_continuous(low='black',
high='red') +
scale_y_log2( name='Period ( years )' ) +
scale_x_datetime(limits=c(min(wave.frame
$time),max(wave.frame$time))) +
scale_alpha( breaks=c(0,1),
labels=c('invalid','valid'), limits=c(-2,1) )
gg.wave

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: wavelet transform plot
parts:
Hi, try this:

TransRevLog2 <- Trans$new("revlog2", function(x) -(log(x, 2)),
function(x) 2^(-x), function(x) bquote(2^.(-x)))

siglvl <- .95
gg.wave <- ggplot( wave.frame ) +
geom_tile( aes(x=time, y=period, fill=power, alpha=coi)) +

geom_contour( aes(x=time, y=period, z=signif), color='white', breaks=siglvl ) +
scale_fill_continuous(low="black", high="red") +

scale_y_continuous( name='Period ( years )', trans="RevLog2") +
scale_x_datetime(limits=c(min(wave.frame$time),max(wave.frame$time))) +
scale_alpha( breaks=c(0,1), labels=c('invalid','valid'), limits=c(-2,1) ) +
opts(panel.grid.minor=theme_blank())
gg.wave


1) define log2-reverse transformer and use it.
2) stop specifying "size" and "colour"
3) detele minor grid.
--

parts:
Hi,

I got the same vertical lines.
And when I changed the size of window, sometimes the lines eliminated and sometimes they appeared at different location.
If you specified colour in aes, then the unexpected lines never appears.

So, my inspection is that this is because of a kind of rounding problem of floating point numerics.
Generally, it is not easy to fix this problem.

Currently, this may be the best:

# convert date to numeric

wave.frame$time2 <-  as.numeric(format.Date(wave.frame$time, "%Y"))
gg.wave <- ggplot( wave.frame ) +

geom_tile( aes(x=time2, y=period, fill=power, alpha=coi)) +

 geom_contour( aes(x=time2, y=period, z=signif), color='white', breaks=siglvl ) +

scale_fill_continuous(low="black", high="red") +

 scale_y_continuous( name='Period ( years )', trans="RevLog2") +

scale_alpha( breaks=c(0,1), labels=c('invalid','valid'), limits=c(-2,1) ) +

 opts(panel.grid.minor=theme_blank())

--

messages.author: daf017f67eba24e8
messages.subject: Re: wavelet transform plot
parts:
thanks for you help, koshke! it's now looking like what I want.

posix and tile dont seem to play well. in retrospect, i guess this should be obvious.  your suggestion works for yearly data, but a tad of extra trickery is necessary for more frequent data. instead of doing it the way you suggested, i opted to retain POSIXct while was being more careful with my POSIXct definitions (down to the second). This also solved the problem with a simple function (I'll paste that code at the end).

for curiosity sake and backing up a bit, should I expect to always define transformers in the global environment?

much appreciated, 

James

## name: evenPOSIXct
## purpose: to make an evenly spaced POSIXct timeseries.

## ts - either:
##              a year.fraction timeseries *with potential gaps*
##              (e.g. c(1980.0, 1980.25, 1980.75, 1981.0) )
##      OR when used with origin and dY:
##              the length of an origin+dY generated timseries.
## origin, dY - must be supplied together
##      origin is a single year.fraction
##      dY - is the fraction of a year of the timestep.
## tz - the timezone for POSIXct class, set to default GMT 
##      instead of the

evenPOSIXct <- function( ts , origin=NULL, dY=NULL, tz='GMT' ) {

  nts <- length(ts) 
  if (nts==1) {
    if (missing(origin) | missing(dY))
      warning('Both origin and dY required for scalar first argument', immediate.=TRUE)
    ts <- origin + ( (0:(ts-1))*dY )
    nts <- length(ts)
  }

  y <- floor(ts) ; f <- ts-y  ## y.f

  ## now need to get the number of seconds in each year
  nsec=as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime(paste('01/01',y+1,sep='/'),format='%d/%m/%Y'),tz=tz)) -
        as.numeric(as.POSIXct(strptime(paste('01/01',y,sep='/'),format='%d/%m/%Y'),tz=tz))

  invisible(as.POSIXct(strptime(paste('01/01',y,sep='/'),
                       format='%d/%m/%Y'),tz=tz) + (nsec * f))
  
}
